source_text: Cauenda sunt autem non solum quae sunt aperta adque manifesta sed et astutae fraudis subtilitate fallentia. quid uero astutius quidue subtilius, quam ut Christi aduentu detectus ac prostratus inimicus, postquam lux gentibus uenit et sospitandis hominibus salutare lumen effulsit, ut surdi auditum gratiae spiritalis admitterent, aperirent ad Dominum oculos caeci, infirmi aeterna sanitate reualescerent, clodi ad ecclesiam currerent, muti claris uocibus et precibus orarent, uidens ille idola derelicta et per nimium credentium populum sedes suas et templa deserta excogitauerit nonam fraudem, ut sub ipso christiani nominis titulo fallat incautos? haereses inuenit et schismata, quibus subuerteret fidem, ueritatem corrumperet, scinderet unitatem. quos detinere non potest in uiae ueteris caecitate circumscribit et decipit noui itineris errore. rapit de ipsa ecclesia homines et, dum sibi adpropinquasse iam lumini adque euasisse saeculi noctem uidentur, alias nescientibus tenebras rursus infundit, ut cum euangelio Christi et cum obseruatione eius et lege non stantes christianos se uocent et ambulantes in tenebris habere se lumen existiment blandiente aduersario adque fallente, qui secundum apostoli uocem transfigurat se uelut angelum lucis et ministros subornat suos uelut ministros iustitiae adserentes noctem pro die, interitum pro salute, desperationem sub obtentu spei, perfidiam sub praetexto fidei, antichristum sub uocabulo Christi, ut dum uerisimilia mentiuntur, ueritatem subtilitate frustrentur. hoc eo fit, fratres dilectissimi, dum ad ueritatis originem non reditur nec caput quaeritur nec magisterii caelestis doctrina seruatur.
thought_title: The devil's new fraud: heresies and schisms under the name of Christ
orientation: Cyprian is warning the faithful that the devil, defeated by Christ's coming, now deceives people under the very name of Christian through heresies and schisms.
pass_a_gloss: But not only the things that are open and manifest must be avoided, but also the things that deceive by the subtlety of cunning fraud. What indeed is more cunning or what is more subtle, than that the enemy, detected and laid low by the coming of Christ, after the light came to the gentiles and the saving light shone forth for men to be saved, so that the deaf might admit the hearing of spiritual grace, the blind might open their eyes to the Lord, the weak might grow strong with eternal health, the lame might run to the Church, the mute might pray with clear voices and prayers, seeing the idols abandoned and his seats and temples deserted because of the excessive number of the believing people, he devised a new fraud, so that under the very title of the Christian name he might deceive the unwary? He invented heresies and schisms, by which he might overthrow faith, corrupt truth, split unity. Those whom he cannot hold in the blindness of the old way he circumscribes and deceives with the error of a new journey. He snatches men from the Church itself and, while they seem to themselves to have already drawn near to the light and to have escaped the night of the world, he pours other darknesses again upon them unawares, so that, not standing with the gospel of Christ and with his observance and law, they call themselves Christians and, walking in darkness, they think that they have light, while the adversary flatters and deceives, who according to the voice of the apostle transforms himself as an angel of light and equips his ministers as ministers of righteousness, asserting night for day, destruction for salvation, despair under the guise of hope, faithlessness under the pretext of faith, antichrist under the name of Christ, so that while he lies with plausible things, he frustrates the truth by subtlety. This happens for this reason, most beloved brethren, because there is no return to the origin of truth, nor is the head sought, nor is the teaching of the heavenly master kept.

choices.why: The subject is the devil (inimicus), continuing the singular agency of the whole passage; 'inuenit' is active invention, not discovery.

choices.english: under the very title of the Christian name
choices.why: 'titulo' here means the label or designation, and 'ipso' emphasizes the very title itself; this captures the deceptive use of the name 'Christian'.
rejected: under the title of the Christian name
under the very name of Christian

choices.term: quos detinere non potest in uiae ueteris caecitate
choices.english: Those whom he cannot hold in the blindness of the old way
choices.why: 'uiae ueteris' is the old way of idolatry and ignorance; 'caecitate' is the blindness of that way; the relative clause keeps the devil as subject.
rejected: whom he cannot detain in the blindness of the old road

choices.english: while he lies with plausible things
choices.why: The subject is singular 'he' (the adversary/devil), not plural; the deponent 'mentiuntur' is third person singular passive form used actively; 'uerisimilia' is neuter plural accusative as the thing lied.
rejected: while they lie with plausible things

choices.english: the teaching of the heavenly master
choices.why: 'magisterii caelestis' is a genitive phrase meaning 'of the heavenly master/teaching authority'; 'doctrina' is the teaching itself; this preserves the genitive relationship.
rejected: the heavenly teaching of the master

bible_refs.note: ministros subornat suos uelut ministros iustitiae

pass_b_english: But we must avoid not only what is open and obvious, but also what deceives through the subtlety of cunning fraud. What could be more cunning or more subtle than this? After the enemy was exposed and laid low by Christ's coming, after light came to the nations and the saving radiance shone forth to rescue humanity—so that the deaf might receive the hearing of spiritual grace, the blind might open their eyes to the Lord, the weak might grow strong with eternal health, the lame might run to the Church, and the mute might pray with clear voices and petitions—he saw the idols abandoned and his seats and temples deserted because of the great number of believers, and so he devised a new fraud: to deceive the unwary under the very title of the Christian name. He invented heresies and schisms, by which he might overthrow faith, corrupt truth, and split unity. Those whom he cannot hold in the blindness of the old way, he circumscribes and deceives with the error of a new journey. He snatches people from the Church itself, and while they seem to have already drawn near to the light and escaped the night of the world, he pours other darkness upon them unawares. So they do not stand with the gospel of Christ and with his observance and law, yet they call themselves Christians; they walk in darkness and think they possess light, because the adversary flatters and deceives them. According to the apostle's word, he transforms himself into an angel of light and equips his ministers as ministers of righteousness, asserting night for day, destruction for salvation, despair under the guise of hope, faithlessness under the pretext of faith, antichrist under the name of Christ—so that while he lies with plausible things, he frustrates truth by subtlety. This happens, most beloved brothers, as long as there is no return to the origin of truth, the head is not sought, and the teaching of the heavenly master is not kept.

problems.source_quote: dum ad ueritatis originem non reditur
problems.why: English states cause as fact; Latin 'dum' indicates ongoing condition ('while/as long as').
problems.fix: This happens, most beloved brothers, as long as there is no return
problems.ruling: 'dum' + 'non reditur' is temporal/conditional 'while/as long as'; 'because' states causal fact, shifting meaning.

edits.old: This happens, most beloved brothers, because there is no return
edits.new: This happens, most beloved brothers, as long as there is no return

fixed: Changed 'because there is no return' to 'as long as there is no return' to render the ongoing condition of Latin 'dum' rather than a statement of cause.

last_rejected.why: Subject 'ille' is the enemy (inimicus), not Christ; English 'he' ambiguously refers to Christ due to prior clause structure.
last_rejected.fix: the enemy saw the idols abandoned
last_rejected.ruling: 'ille' clearly refers to 'inimicus'; 'he' grammatically continues that subject. No real ambiguity for careful readers.

last_rejected.quote: as long as there is no return
last_rejected.source_quote: dum ad ueritatis originem non reditur
last_rejected.why: Latin 'dum' with present indicative describes actual ongoing cause, not merely temporal 'as long as'; 'fit' = 'this happens because'.
last_rejected.fix: This happens, most beloved brothers, because we do not return to the origin of truth
last_rejected.ruling: 'as long as' correctly renders causal-temporal 'dum' with present indicative; 'this happens' already conveys 'fit' as cause.
